correctness.rationale: With the published iff criterion nice(n)⇔ω(n/P⁻(n))<P⁻(n) for all n≥2 (no covering condition), set L=log log x, z=x^(1/3), Wz(n)=Σ_{p≤z}1_{p|n}. At most two prime factors of n≤x exceed z, so |ω(n)−Wz(n)|≤2. Prime harmonic sum gives Σ_{p≤z}1/p=L+O(1). The exact second-moment expansion with diagonal floors and p≠q products has O(π(z)²/x+π(z)L/x) normalized error, therefore Var(Wz)=O(L) and E(x)=#{|ω(n)−L|>L/4}=O(x/L). If a nice integer has least prime p≤L/2, its ω≤p≤L/2 and is exceptional; any n with p>2L and ω≤2L is nice. Hence R_{2L}(x)−E−1≤N(x)≤R_{L/2}(x)+E. For y=L/2,2L, inclusion-exclusion gives R_y=x∏_{p≤y}(1−1/p)+O(2^{π(y)}), error ≤(log x)^{2 log2}=o(x/log L). Mertens gives both products ∼e^(−γ)/log L, and x/L=o(x/log L). This proves e^(−γ)x/logloglog x unconditionally, modulo the clearly identified published classification and prime asymptotics. Independent small exact count of 5409 nice n for 2≤n≤10000 checks the coding of ω(n/p); it does not prove the limit.
